segments.title: Chương 198: 0198【Xào Nấu Khái Niệm Weibo】
segments.content:
Chapter 201: Hype the Weibo Concept (Bonus Chapter for Alliance Lord Chang'an Xiaocaizi)

Chen Guiliang adjusted the microphone height. "Hello everyone, my name is Chen Guiliang, founder of ByteDance."

"ByteDance currently has three websites: Xiaonei, Kaixin, and Kaixin Bazaar... Mr. Jin from Cyworld China just detailed their specific functions..."

"I'm very pleased that the original Korean Cyworld has evolved to the point where users can send updates to each other's phones... Perhaps great minds think alike. Cyworld's 'Cymessage' is actually Kaixin's 'Weibo.' Moreover, they were launched at around the same time, so there's no question of who copied whom."

No matter how much Chen Guiliang disliked the Koreans, and even if Cyworld was a competitor, he had to be amicable at a time like this. Make the pie bigger together!

Because "Weibo," or rather, "Cymessage," was an absolutely new thing. One more pioneer could accelerate the market's growth.

After making the pie bigger side by side, it wouldn't be out of the question to fight to the death.

What's more, Kaixin currently held an absolute advantage.

Chen Guiliang continued, "I just heard Mr. Jin say that Cyworld in Korea has already become profitable, with daily revenues of 300,000 USD. Even 'Mobile Cyworld' and 'Cymessage' have a considerable number of users. This gives me even more confidence..."

These words were meant for investors and media reporters.

Their Korean counterpart was already making money. The market in China was much larger, so it was only a matter of time before Kaixin and Weibo would also become profitable.

Chen Guiliang said, "As of yesterday afternoon, the number of users who have activated the mobile Weibo function has increased to over 2,900. Over the past half a month, it has been growing at an average rate of 120 people per day. As more and more celebrities join, this speed will accelerate. I believe that by next summer, the number of paying Weibo users will reach 50,000!"

"It's not just celebrities. Ordinary paying users have also started posting on Weibo, recording and sharing their lives anytime, anywhere..."

"In addition to monthly SMS and MMS services, we will also be launching a gift-giving feature..."

"What SNS websites lack now is not users, but ways to monetize and profit. I believe Weibo is a very good exploration in this direction. I hope that websites like Sina Blog and Bokee can also launch Weibo features. Let's all work together to make this pie bigger..."

Making the pie bigger together, my ass. Chen Guiliang was purely hyping the Weibo concept.

Once the concept was heated up and more people knew about it, the number of paying users for Kaixin Weibo would grow faster.

In fact, the representatives of the small and medium-sized companies who came to speak today had similar ideas to Chen Guiliang. They were either promoting their own websites or hyping a certain business concept.

Offstage.

Chen Tianqiao asked Ding San Shi, "What exactly are this Cymessage and Weibo? I don't quite understand."

"It might be a brand new wireless value-added service." Ding San Shi didn't quite understand either, as neither of them had used an SNS website.

The internet changed every year. Compared to the young people of today, they were already a bit "out of date."

Sina CEO Wang Yan was lost in thought, planning to go back and have his team research whether they could launch a mobile version of Sina Blog. Just call it Sina Weibo!

Right now, Sina Blog was burning through money like crazy, without a single cent of profit to show for it.

Cyworld's Kim Hee-yong, however, was a little frustrated.

After coming to China and facing his number one competitor, Kaixin, Kim Hee-yong had been studying it seriously.

He was surprised to find that Xiaonei and Cyworld had identical functions. It was just that Xiaonei only served the student community.

And Kaixin, while seemingly similar, had actually carved out a different path: following strangers!

This feature of following strangers was very beneficial for attracting celebrities from all walks of life, and it could also expand the social circles of ordinary people.

Take "Cymessage" for instance; only a user's friends could see it. But a "Weibo" post could be sent to all the fans who were closely following you!

When Kim Hee-yong first came to China, he was a bit arrogant, thinking he was a max-level character entering a novice village.

But he quickly put aside his arrogance and even wrote a ten-thousand-word report to headquarters, hoping that Cyworld (China) could also adopt this model.

The Korean headquarters absolutely refused to approve it.

They even gave him a harsh scolding, telling him to obediently replicate the Korean model in China.

Bokee CEO Fang Xindong watched Chen Guiliang speak eloquently with a blank expression.

He had already gone too far to stop, having successively launched projects like a search engine and an email service. In the short term, he had neither the money nor the energy to develop a Weibo-like feature.

He was very lost now; all his new projects were failing to gain traction!

But on the surface, he still looked glamorous. Bokee's market share was firmly above 60% (it was 70% two months ago). The absolute industry leader.

The ones who had been crushed by Sina Blog were the dozens of other small and medium-sized blog sites.

The problem was, that damn Sohu had also jumped in, launching Sohu Blog a few days ago. Charles Zhang had also invited a large number of business celebrities, who flocked to Sohu to write blogs.

What was sure to follow was a three-way standoff.

*Clap clap clap clap!*

A round of applause broke out, and Chen Guiliang stepped down from the stage.

The vice president of China Pages walked up to the stage with a smile and began a long, rambling speech. It was like an industry report, making people drowsy.

So far, his speech was the second longest.

The longest speech was given by the CEO of Wangku Pages, who even continued speaking after his time was up.

Finally, they reached the media interview session, and a bunch of top-tier big shots immediately bailed.

Only Charles Zhang voluntarily stayed behind, so a large number of media outlets went to interview him.

"You should attend the group forum tomorrow. I won't be coming," Chen Guiliang said to Ao Yanchen.

Ao Yanchen pointed at the group of big shots who were leaving and teased with a smile, "I understand. The real big shots only need to show up on the first day."

Chen Guiliang was already used to Senior Sister Ao's sharp tongue.

"Hello, Mr. Chen. I'm Li Jun, a reporter from China Internet Weekly." A middle-aged reporter walked over.

"Hello."

"First of all, congratulations, Mr. Chen. ByteDance has been selected for the '2005 Top 100 Internet Innovations'."

"Thank you."

It was the end of the year, and all sorts of lists were being released.

This "2005 Top 100 Internet Innovations" was a list compiled by China Internet Weekly.

Chen Guiliang didn't need to go and receive an award; it was announced directly in the magazine.

Li Jun said, "Our focus this time is on internet innovation. Kaixin's mobile Weibo feature is a clear example of innovation. How did you come up with a product like Weibo, Mr. Chen?"

With the media proactively helping to promote Weibo, Chen Guiliang was naturally pleased. "Blogs allow ordinary netizens to share their articles and lives. But blogs ultimately require a computer, and you can't carry a computer with you everywhere."

"Laptops you can," Li Jun said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang said, "For example, if I'm walking down the street and see Fan Bingbing fighting with Xu Jinglei, I can't just take out my laptop to write a blog post. That's when I can use mobile Weibo. I can take out my phone, snap a picture of them pulling each other's hair, and then write a short description of twenty to thirty words. A minute later, all my followers could potentially see it."

Ao Yanchen sat beside him, covering her mouth to stifle a laugh.

What an example. Fan Bingbing and Xu Jinglei pulling each other's hair on the street, for god's sake!

Li Jun was also amused. "I'm going to publish this verbatim, you know."

"I was just giving an example. We could change it to Li Yunlong versus Lü Fengxian," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Jun said, "Mr. Chen, you're very humorous. Do you think this model can be sustained long-term?"

"As mobile phones and communication technology improve, Weibo will definitely become more and more popular."

"Will it rely solely on celebrities to drive it?"

"Of course not. Celebrities are just for initial guidance. Among ordinary users, they are also starting to interact with each other using Weibo."

After a few more exchanges, Li Jun left.
